chunks: Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah does not forgive that which is associated with Him, and He forgives what is below that for whom He wills. The major sins, and what is besides them. I said, 'Do the major sins fall within the exception?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ: that partners are associated with Him

ai.seo_question: Are major sins included in the exception of Allah's forgiveness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the scope of Allah's forgiveness by distinguishing between Shirk, which is excluded, and all other sins, including the major sins (al-Kaba'ir), which fall within the realm of divine will. It resolves a common theological nuance by confirming that major sins are not automatically unforgiven but are subject to Allah's discretion, either through His mercy or His justice. This aligns with the Shia understanding of the interplay between divine mercy and the necessity of repentance for major transgressions.

en.hubeali:
Yunus, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Forgive if associated with and He<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives what is besides that to the one whom He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to of the major sins and what is besides that’. I said, ‘Are the major sins included in the exception?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 18. Yunus has narrated from ibn Bukayr from Sulayman ibn Khalid from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Imam said that Allah has said, ‘Allah does not forgive the sin of considering others equal to Him, however. He may grant exceptions in other forms of sins that He may choose to forgive, . . .’ [4:48] It is a reference to the major sins and the lesser sins.”
I (the narrator) asked the Imam, ‘Does the above exception apply to any of one’s major sins?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, it does apply to the major sins.’”
